I farm 20 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the same 20 mu for winter wheat and then summer maize. I have 25 years of experience, I know my land, and I have well irrigation, so I will manage for stable yield rather than take big risks. Because some family members work off-farm, I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better yield, use moderate fertilizer, and rely on a few irrigations if rainfall is not enough. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my rotation and fits my labor situation. My goal is steady production, manageable costs, and low risk on both crops.
